## Set Up

```{r}
library(tidyverse) # general use
library(janitor) # cleaning data 
library(here) # data organization 
library(lubridate) # date and time 
library(naniar) # to use gg_miss_var

# reading in biomass data
biomass <- read.csv(here("data", 
                      "annual_all_species_fish.csv"),
                 # changing -99999 values to be na
                 na = "-99999")
# reading in sea surface temperature data for if I want to use it
sst <- read.csv(here("data", "SST_update2023.csv"))

# reading in bottom temperature data 
bottom_temp <- read.csv(here("data", "Bottom_temp_all_years.csv"),
                        # changing -99999 values to be na
                        na = "-99999")
```

### Visualize Missing Data 

```{r}
#| label: visualizing-missing-biomass-data

# looking at the missing biomass data
biomass |> 
  # cleaning names
  clean_names() |> 
  # filter for desired species
  filter(common_name %in% c("California Sheephead", 
                            "Red Urchin", 
                            "Purple Urchin", 
                            "Giant Kelp")) |>
  # selecting for dry mass and common name
  select(dry_gm2, common_name) |> 
  # using gg_miss_var to check for "na" data for species
  gg_miss_var(facet = common_name)
```

```{r}
#| label: visualizing-missing-biomass-data

# looking at the missing temperature data
bottom_temp |> 
  clean_names() |> 
  # filter for fish
  select(temp_c) |> 
  # using gg_miss_var to check for "na" data
  gg_miss_var()
```

### Time Series with full_join

#### Clean Data 

```{r}
#| label: cleaning-data

# BIOMASS

# creating new object, biomass_clean
biomass_clean <- biomass |> 
  # cleaning names
  clean_names() |>  
  # filtering for desired species 
  filter(common_name %in% c("California Sheephead", 
                            "Red Urchin", 
                            "Purple Urchin", 
                            "Giant Kelp")) |> 
  # renaming date
  rename(original_date = date) |>  
  # using mutate and lubridate to convert original_date 
  # into new date column that can be used to create time series
  mutate(
    date = ymd(original_date),
    year = floor_date(date, unit = "year")) |>
  # dropping na values to use summarize
  drop_na(dry_gm2) |> 
  # grouping data by year and species
  group_by(year,
           common_name) |> 
  # using summarize to get the mean dry biomass and make one row per year
  summarize(mean_dry_gm2 = mean(dry_gm2)) |> 
  # ungrouping data 
  ungroup() |> 
  # relocating columns to left to look at
  relocate(common_name, year, mean_dry_gm2)

# TEMPERATURE

# creating new object to look at temperature data
bottom_temp_clean <- bottom_temp |> 
  # cleaning names
  clean_names() |>  
  # using mutate and lubridate to convert date_local
  # into new date column that can be used to create time series
  mutate(
    date = ymd(date_local),
    year = floor_date(date, unit = "year")) |>
  # grouping data by year
  group_by(year) |> 
  # using summarize to get mean temp and make one row per year
  summarize(mean_temp_c = mean(temp_c)) |> 
  # ungrouping the data 
  ungroup() |> 
  # relocating desired columns to left side
  relocate(year, mean_temp_c) 
```

#### Joining Datasets


```{r}
#| label: joining-datasets

# creating new object to join datasets
biomass_bottom_temp <- full_join(
  biomass_clean,
  bottom_temp_clean,
  # joining datasets by year
  by = c("year"))
```

#### Looking at CA Sheephead, Giant Kelp, and Red and Purple Urchins through time

```{r}
#| label: visualizing-species-abundance-through-time

# species mean dry biomass timeseries NO FACET

# base layer: ggplot
ggplot(biomass_bottom_temp) + 
  # year on x axis, biomass on y axis, coloring by species
  aes(x = year,
      y = mean_dry_gm2, 
      color = common_name) + 
  # first layer: geom_line
  geom_line() + 
  # second layer: geom_point
  geom_point(size = 0.5) + 
    # customizing x axis year labels for every 3 years
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 years", 
               date_labels = "%Y") + 
  # customizing colors
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Giant Kelp" = "seagreen",
    "California Sheephead" = "dodgerblue4",
    "Purple Urchin" = "purple",
    "Red Urchin" = "firebrick")) + 
  # using labs to label axes
  labs(
    x = "Time (years)",
    y = "Mean dry biomass (g/m^2)") +
  # adding custom theme 
  theme_minimal() +
  # removing axis
  theme(legend.position = "NONE")
```

```{r}
# species mean dry biomass timeseries FACET

# base layer: ggplot
ggplot(biomass_bottom_temp) + 
  # year on x axis, biomass on y axis, coloring by species
  aes(x = year,
      y = mean_dry_gm2, 
      color = common_name) + 
  # first layer: geom_line
  geom_line() + 
  # second layer: geom_point
  geom_point(size = 0.5) + 
  # faceting by species
  facet_wrap(~ common_name,
             # letting y axis adjust for each species 
             scales = "free_y", 
             # putting in one column for better viewing 
             ncol = 1) + 
    # customizing x axis year labels for every 3 years
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 years", 
               date_labels = "%Y") + 
  # customizing colors
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Giant Kelp" = "seagreen",
    "California Sheephead" = "dodgerblue4",
    "Purple Urchin" = "purple",
    "Red Urchin" = "firebrick")) + 
  # using labs to label axes
  labs(
    x = "Time (years)",
    y = "Mean dry biomass (g/m^2)") +
  # adding custom theme 
  theme_minimal() +
  # removing axis
  theme(legend.position = "NONE")
```
#### Looking at temperature (celsius) through time 

```{r}
# time series mean temperature 

# base layer: ggplot
ggplot(biomass_bottom_temp) + 
  # x axis year, y axis mean temperature
  aes(x = year,
      y = mean_temp_c) + 
  # first layer: geom_line
  # custom color for line
  geom_line(color = "sienna2") + 
  # second layer: geom_point
  # custom color and adjusting size
  geom_point(
    color = "sienna2",
    size = 0.5) + 
  # customizing x axis year labels for every 3 years
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 years", 
               date_labels = "%Y") + 
  # using labs to label x and y axis 
  labs(
    x = "Time (years)",
    y = "Temperature (celcius)") +
  # custom theme
  theme_minimal()
```

### CA Sheephead versus purple urchin abundance 

#### Clean data

```{r}
#| label: cleaning-urchin-and-sheephead-data

# creating new object to look compare sheephead and urchin biomass
sheephead_and_urchin <- biomass |> 
  # clean names
  clean_names() |>  
  # filtering by urchin and sheephead
  filter(common_name %in% c("California Sheephead", 
                            "Purple Urchin")) |> 
  # renaming date for lubridate adjustment
  rename(original_date = date) |>  
  # using mutate and lubridate to convert original_date
  # into new date column to look at by year
  mutate(
    date = ymd(original_date),
    year = floor_date(date, unit = "year")) |>
  # dropping missing dry_gm2 values
  drop_na(dry_gm2) |> 
  # grouping by year and common_name
  group_by(year,
           common_name) |> 
  # using summarize to find mean dry_gm2 and make one row per year
  summarize(mean_dry_gm2 = mean(dry_gm2)) |> 
  # ungrouping
  ungroup() |> 
  # using pivot_wider to look at CA sheephead and urchin as columns with values from mean_dry_gm2
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = common_name,
    values_from = mean_dry_gm2) |> 
  # cleaning names
  clean_names()
```

#### CA Sheephead vs Purple Urchin abundance

```{r}
#| label: visualizing-urchin-and-sheephead-data

# base layer: ggplot
ggplot(sheephead_and_urchin) + 
  # looking at CA sheephead biomass on x axis, purple urchin on y
  aes(x = california_sheephead,
           # y-axis: abundance
           y = purple_urchin) + 
  # second layer: geom_point
  geom_point() + 
  # using labs to label axes
  labs(
    x = "California sheephead mean dry biomass (g/m^2)",
    y = "Purple urchin mean dry biomass (g/m^2)") +
  # custom theme
  theme_minimal()
```
